subject: Private Nexus connectivity: allowlist requirements and verification plan
messages:
From: Jim Phillips <jim@aurorahealth.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Network Ops - Aurora Health <netops@aurorahealth.com>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private Nexus connectivity: allowlist requirements and verification plan

Hi Laura / Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier this week. We're lining up our networking team to do the allowlist and firewall work for the on-prem Private Nexus deployment. Before they start, they asked for a single, concise artifact outlining exactly what to allow and what to expect during the first verification test.

Specifically, can you provide:  
- The minimal set of outbound IPs and ports that must be permitted from our edge (NAT) to Redwood's control plane and telemetry endpoints.
- Whether DNS names are sufficient in lieu of fixed IPs (we have strict change control).
- Guidance on TLS fingerprints / cert authorities we should pin (if any).
- Recommended approach for egress to S3-compatible storage (we plan to use an internal object gateway) and KMS endpoints for key wrapping.
- A short test checklist we can run with NetOps (smoke tests + packet captures).

We're under a compressed procurement window so a one-page checklist + expected IP list would be ideal. Can someone from your side also confirm whether temporary IP rotation during our rollout will require a new RFC / change window on our side?

Thanks,
Jim
Jim Phillips
Infrastructure Lead, Aurora Health

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Jim Phillips <jim@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 08:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private Nexus connectivity: allowlist requirements and verification plan

Jim — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a concise expectations PDF and the connectivity diagram for your network team. High level answers up front, then the checklist below.

High level:
- We publish a stable set of egress IPs for our control plane (see attachment) that are stable for monthly windows; exceptional rotations are communicated 30 days ahead where possible.
- DNS names are acceptable for short-term validation, but for production gating we require IPs in your appliance allowlist (many corporate firewalls do not resolve at scale during boot).
- All traffic to Redwood control plane and telemetry is TLS 1.2+ (we recommend TLS 1.3). We rotate certs via Let's Encrypt / internal authority chain; we do not support CA pinning on our side — instead rely on standard public CAs and OCSP stapling.
- For object storage: if you front the connection with an internal S3 gateway, allow outbound HTTPS to your gateway plus the Redwood ingestion endpoint (listed). If you use external S3, we will provide signed upload URLs and require HTTPS only. KMS calls must reach your managed KMS; we never send raw keys offsite.
- Temporary IP rotation: if rotation is within our published ephemeral block (see doc) and your firewall accepts DNS name fallback, no RFC is needed for short tests. For production changes we recommend a maintenance window so NetOps can validate.

Quick test checklist (smoke):
1) From your NAT egress IP, curl --resolve against the control-plane hostname (verify 200 + TLS cert CN).
2) Attempt a model-inference handshake using test tokens (we will provide) — confirm 101/streaming start.
3) Upload a 1MB file via signed ingest URL (verify 200 and audit log event).
4) Confirm KMS key-wrapping flow (local log + Redwood ack).
5) Packet capture of the initial TLS handshake to confirm SNI and cert chain.
6) Verify telemetry ingestion acceptance on 443 and that no TCP RSTs occur from middlebox.

I've also included an IP appendix (short) in the attached PDF. If NetOps wants to avoid per-change RFCs, toggling to DNS-based validation for the rollout window is the pragmatic route; we can provide a signed list and a verification webhook.

Next steps: can you share a preferred 2-hour test window next week? Ben, can you own the test liaison and be on the call for any on-the-fly allowlist tweaks? Marissa, please see note on runbook below.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
(415) 555-0148

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com

Laura / Ben — quick internal coordination note before the test:

Proposed engagement sequence (internal):
- Day -3: Share signed IP list + DNS fallback webhook (we'll upload to the Drive link).
- Day -1: Runbook validation with Aurora NetOps (dry run of each smoke step).
- Day 0: Live 2-hour window for smoke + extended ingestion test. We keep a rolling 30-minute rollback checkpoint.
- Day +1: Confirm audit events, hand over logs for SOC acceptance.

Operational ownership: Ben (test liaison / firewall tweaks), Laura (runbook and verification tokens), Marissa (contract / procurement liaison — ensure Docusign envelope has the final annex for IP stewardship).

Notes/risks:
- Some customers run deep-packet inspection appliances that will break streaming handshakes (we should include a troubleshooting KB for that).
- If Aurora insists on full IP pinning we need a signed change control annex — that adds a 2-week lead time for internal ops to reserve static blocks.

I'll prepare the runbook (network-test-runbook-v2.odt) and seed the Drive doc. Ben — can you confirm you can be on the test call Friday 2027-05-21 09:00 PT?

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Solutions
